Contributing to RdistNN

Source: CONTRIBUTING.md

Supported workflows include CATE, nonparametric regression, supplied-prediction CLATE and ordinary paired-signal ratios, with shared weights, tuning, diagnostics, reporting and plots. Optional ratio confidence-set inversion, all PLQR functionality and local IV-GMM remain experimental. Please open an issue before proposing a new estimator or a change to an exported interface.

Development and production workflow

Use the local development branch for ongoing work. It has no upstream until publication is authorized. GitHub cannot make an individual branch private in a public repository; keeping development local preserves its unpublished state. Commit development changes there, with focused tests and documentation.

When the maintainer authorizes a production update, publish a review branch and open a pull request targeting master. Include the problem, final behavior and verification in the description. Complete the required CI checks and review, then squash-merge the PR so production history records the reviewed change rather than each intermediate development commit. Do not push directly to master without an explicit override. Keep local development current with the reviewed production state before starting the next change.

R and Stata parity

Use R as the numerical reference for shared estimator behavior. The companion Stata package retains its own command grammar, while reporting, candidate reuse and saved-fit prediction should agree on frozen observations/signals, fixed training geometry, weight normalization, covariance scale and undefined CLATE targets. PLQR parity currently concerns moments at supplied coefficients; Stata does not provide R’s density-backed coefficient inference.

Cross-language regression fixtures and their R generators live in the sibling RdistNN_stata/tests/fixtures/ and RdistNN_stata/tools/ directories. In particular, generate_r_reporting_fixtures.R and generate_r_reuse_fixtures.R record reporting and reusable-fit reference values. Run their matching Stata regressions after an intentional shared-contract change, and retain independent delete-one references rather than accepting agreement between two fast paths alone. Do not regenerate golden values merely to make a failure pass.

The same parity requirement applies within each package: compiled C++, R and Mata paths implement the same selected method. Require exact discrete decisions and justified tolerances for continuous quantities; verify forced engines and automatic fallback separately. The compiled-code policy defines arithmetic and cross-system reproducibility requirements, with coverage specified by the linked testing policy.

Local setup

Use R 4.1.0 or newer and a C++17 toolchain. OpenMP is optional. Install the development tools and package dependencies from the repository root:

install.packages(c("devtools", "pkgdown", "rcmdcheck", "yaml"))
devtools::install_deps(dependencies = TRUE)

Documentation is generated with roxygen2 8.0.0, as declared in DESCRIPTION; use that version to avoid namespace drift. If needed:

install.packages("remotes")  # if not already installed
remotes::install_version("roxygen2", version = "8.0.0", upgrade = "never")

Editing and checking

  • Document exported functions in their R source. Regenerate help with devtools::document(); do not hand-edit NAMESPACE, man/*.Rd, or RcppExports.*.
  • Edit README.Rmd, then run devtools::build_readme().
  • Write small, deterministic examples. Mark oracle quantities explicitly and keep simulation illustrations distinct from manuscript evidence.
  • Preserve matrix and data-frame interfaces, returned fields, and defaults during documentation or packaging changes.
  • Add focused testthat coverage for changes to behavior or validation. Read AGENTS.md and the linked design policies for the detailed contracts.

For package behavior changes, run devtools::test() and relevant focused checks. The test-suite map lists the behavior-based files, shared helpers, focused filters, and optional visual tests. Before a release, run the full package and site builds described in RELEASING.md. Documentation changes should at least execute their changed examples and verify their links and generated output.

The existing alignment checks can be run from the repository root:

Rscript tools/ci/check_tests_declared_deps.R
Rscript tools/ci/check_repository_hygiene.R
Rscript tools/ci/check_pkgdown_reference_coverage.R
Rscript tools/ci/check_generated_file_drift.R
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests/ci -v

The generated-file check includes all roxygen Rd topics and rejects missing or obsolete generated files. It runs in isolation and uses the roxygen2 version in DESCRIPTION. Repository hygiene covers staged and new candidate files; keep verification output under ignored build/ or archives/ directories. The same hygiene gate rejects duplicate top-level function definitions across R modules; function-local closures may reuse names. Give each shared function one implementation owner so source-loading order cannot choose its behavior. With both checkouts present, verify shared native headers explicitly with python3 ../RdistNN_stata/tools/ci/package_hygiene.py --r-root ..

Maintainer reference

The design index routes interface, validation, numerical and engineering contracts. The result architecture explains shared generic dispatch and method-specific adapters; the paired-ratio contract records CLATE signal, covariance and numerical-status requirements. Package scope distinguishes implemented capabilities from extensions requiring further justification.

Public maintainer documentation should explain current decisions, scientific limits and reproducible development procedures. Keep personal source-library configuration, session instructions, completed task lists and local execution receipts in private working records. Local archives/ is ignored and excluded from R source packages; check that private records are untracked before committing.

Reporting problems

Open an issue with a minimal reproducible example, the expected and actual results, and sessionInfo(). For numerical discrepancies, also report whether they persist with options(RdistNN.use_compiled = FALSE). That selects supported R algorithms; it does not remove the compiler requirement for source installation.

For a pull request, describe the concrete change, its scope, and the checks run. Update NEWS.md for user-visible changes. Exclude generated check directories, source archives, rendered site files, and harvested CI logs from commits.
